subject: english
question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

I don't mind trying to make your day as well as you make mine.

options.text: as well as you make mine

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the** incorrect comparison** between "make your day" and "make mine."
 
• The phrase should be corrected to "I don't mind trying to make your day **as you make mine**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I don't mind trying to make your day** as you make mine**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1) "I don't mind trying,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2) "to make your day,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3) "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 4.
